title: [F-01] DB migration system
description:
Implement a versioned migration system for the SQLite schema. Currently any schema change risks corrupting existing user installs. Required before any IDE integration or team/cloud schema additions. Should run automatically on startup and be idempotent.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Migration files versioned in `src/db/migrations/`
- Runs on every startup, skips already-applied migrations
- Rolls back cleanly on failure
- Existing installs upgrade without data loss
label: bug

title: [F-02] Midnight session split
description:
Sessions that span midnight (e.g. 11pm–1am) are attributed entirely to the start date, causing the next day to show missing activity and the previous day to be inflated.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session grouper splits events at midnight boundary
- Each day gets only the events that occurred within it
- Pure function change in `src/sessions/grouper.ts` with test coverage
label: bug

title: [F-03] Test coverage — events / status / export / sessions CLI
description:
Four CLI commands have zero test coverage: `events.ts`, `status.ts`, `export.ts`, `sessions.ts`. These are user-facing commands that can regress silently.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Unit tests for each command in `tests/cli/`
- Cover happy path and key error states
- No DB imports in test files (mock at boundary)
label: dx

title: [F-04] Fix Node engine version documentation
description:
package.json sets `engines.node >= 22` (required for `node:sqlite`) but README and some docs imply >= 18. This misleads users and causes confusing install failures.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- README, getting-started.md, and package.json all consistently state Node >= 22
- Error message on older Node is clear and actionable
label: dx

title: [P-01] workscribe week — weekly digest command
description:
Add a `workscribe week` command (or `workscribe summary --week` alias) that generates an AI summary of Mon–today for the current week. Useful pre-standup ritual and the natural unit for team reporting.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe week` outputs a markdown summary grouped by day
- Supports `--slack` to post to configured webhook
- Cached in `~/.workscribe/weekly-cache/<YYYY-WW>.md`
- `--fresh` bypasses cache
label: feature

title: [P-02] Annotation support — workscribe note
description:
Add `workscribe note "context"` to let developers attach free-text context to the current session. AI can't infer why you spent 3 hours on a 2-line fix — annotations fill that gap.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe note "Fixed race condition in auth middleware"` appends to current session
- Notes appear in the AI prompt payload
- Notes visible in `workscribe sessions` output
- Stored in DB, not lost on session rebuild
label: feature

title: [P-03] VS Code / Cursor IDE hook
description:
Capture IDE activity (file opens, saves, debug runs) alongside terminal events. The terminal alone misses significant engineering time spent in the editor.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- VS Code extension or workspace settings hook
- Events flow into the same `events` table via `workscribe _capture`
- Category: `ide_session` or per-action category
- Optional — user installs separately, not bundled
label: feature

title: [P-04] Gemini and Groq provider support
description:
Add Google Gemini and Groq as AI providers. Reduces the barrier for users without Anthropic or OpenAI accounts and adds a fast/cheap tier via Groq.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `src/ai/providers/gemini.ts` and `src/ai/providers/groq.ts` implementing `AIProvider`
- Router updated in `src/ai/router.ts`
- Config docs updated
- Default models documented
label: feature

title: [P-05] workscribe undo — session-aware invalidation
description:
Currently `workscribe undo` deletes events from the DB but doesn't invalidate the cached sessions for the affected date. Sessions shown after undo are stale until the event count diverges.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `undo` calls `clearSessionsForDate()` for affected date after deleting events
- Sessions rebuild correctly on next `workscribe sessions` or `workscribe summary`
label: bug

title: [P-06] Email digest — daily summary delivery
description:
Send the daily summary via email so developers get it without opening a terminal. Supports SMTP (self-configured) and optionally SendGrid.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe config set integrations.email user@example.com`
- Triggered manually via `workscribe summary --email` or via cron
- Plain-text and HTML variants
- No email sent if no events captured
label: feature

title: [P-07] Improved init onboarding UX
description:
The current `workscribe init` flow is functional but minimal. First-run experience directly impacts retention — developers who don't see value in the first session churn.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Clear step-by-step output with progress indicators
- Explains what the shell hook does before installing
- Validates API key during init (test call)
- Prints a "what to do next" summary at the end
- Re-run is still safe and idempotent
label: dx

title: [T-01] Cloud backend — user accounts and team workspaces
description:
Design and implement the cloud backend required for all team features. This is the infrastructure foundation for Phase 2.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Auth: email/password + GitHub OAuth
- Team workspace model: one workspace, multiple members
- API accepts summary payloads from CLI
- Deployed and reachable at api.workscribe.co
- Secrets management and env config documented
label: infra

title: [T-02] Secure sync — local to cloud opt-in
description:
Developers must be able to choose what leaves their machine. Opt-in per repo or per session. Non-negotiable for professional adoption.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe sync` command pushes summaries (not raw events) to cloud
- Per-repo opt-out: `workscribe config set sync.exclude '["/path/to/sensitive"]'`
- Raw events never leave the device — only AI summaries sync
- Clear confirmation before first sync
- `--dry-run` shows what would be synced
label: feature

title: [T-03] Slack team digest — daily and weekly rollup
description:
Post a daily or weekly digest to a team Slack channel with per-member summaries. This is the first team touchpoint and the primary organic spread mechanism.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Team admin configures a shared Slack webhook
- Each member's summary is attributed by name
- Daily digest posts automatically at a configured time (cron or manual trigger)
- Opt-out per member
- Formatted for Slack (bold headings, bullet conversion)
label: feature

title: [T-04] Team web dashboard — read-only summary view
description:
A web dashboard where team members and managers can see aggregated work summaries without installing anything.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Auth via invite link or GitHub
- Shows today + last 7 days per member
- Grouped by project/repo
- Mobile-readable
- No raw event data exposed — summaries only
label: feature

title: [T-05] Privacy controls — per-repo and per-session opt-out
description:
Developers must be able to exclude sensitive repos or specific sessions from any cloud sync or team visibility. Without this, adoption in professional teams is blocked.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe privacy exclude /path/to/repo`
- Excluded repos: events captured locally but never synced or summarised in team view
- Session-level: `workscribe pause` already works — ensure paused events are flagged and excluded from sync
- Privacy settings visible in `workscribe status`
label: feature

title: [T-06] Invite flow — workscribe invite
description:
Bottom-up team onboarding. One developer installs, invites teammates without requiring admin involvement.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe invite user@example.com` sends an invite to join the workspace
- Invite email includes install instructions
- Invitee's CLI prompts to join workspace on first sync
- Team admin can revoke invites
label: feature

title: [I-01] GitHub integration — link sessions to PRs and issues
description:
Connect captured terminal sessions to the GitHub PRs and issues they contributed to. Closes the loop between work captured and work shipped.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- GitHub OAuth in cloud backend
- Sessions with `git push` events are linked to the corresponding PR automatically
- PR description can be auto-populated from Workscribe summary
- Team dashboard shows sessions grouped by PR
label: feature

title: [I-02] Linear integration — tag sessions to issues
description:
Link captured sessions to Linear issues. Developers tag sessions; managers see which issues consumed the most real time.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe tag LIN-123` links current session to a Linear issue
- OAuth with Linear API
- Time-on-issue visible in team dashboard
- Linear issue comments optionally updated with session summary
label: feature

title: [I-03] Sprint retrospective generation
description:
Generate a sprint retrospective from actual terminal data rather than from memory. Replaces the "what did we do this sprint" question with a factual answer.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe retro --sprint <start> <end>` generates a markdown retro
- Grouped by team member and project
- Highlights: what shipped, what took longest, blockers (inferred from repeated attempts)
- Exportable to Linear, Notion, or markdown file
label: feature

title: [I-04] Manager aggregate view — trends and bottlenecks
description:
Give engineering managers a view of where time actually goes across the team — by project, by type of work, over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Time breakdown by category (feature, bug, infra, meetings inferred from AI sessions)
- Trend chart: week-over-week per project
- Bottleneck signal: repos with high event density but low commit frequency
- Exportable as PDF or CSV
label: feature

title: [I-05] Jira integration
description:
Enterprise teams require Jira integration for adoption. Link sessions to Jira tickets and surface time-on-ticket data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Jira OAuth (cloud and server)
- `workscribe tag PROJ-456` links session to Jira issue
- Jira issue time-tracking fields optionally updated
- Team dashboard Jira view
label: feature

title: [I-06] workscribe report — sharable engineering time report
description:
Generate a sharable report of engineering time for a period — replaces manual status updates sent to leadership.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `workscribe report --week` / `--month` outputs a formatted markdown or PDF report
- Includes: total time by project, key achievements, open work
- Sharable link via cloud backend
- Team aggregate and individual views
label: feature

title: [E-01] SSO / SAML authentication
description:
Enterprise procurement requires SSO. Without it, large orgs cannot approve Workscribe for team-wide use.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Google Workspace, Azure AD)
- Enforce SSO for workspace (admin setting)
- JIT provisioning of new members on first SSO login
label: infra

title: [E-02] Audit logs
description:
Compliance requirement for enterprise customers — who captured what, what was synced, who accessed it.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Immutable audit log: member activity, sync events, permission changes
- Exportable as CSV
- Retention policy configurable (90/180/365 days)
- Accessible by workspace admin only
label: infra

title: [E-03] On-prem and self-hosted cloud tier
description:
Security-sensitive orgs won't send any data to a SaaS. Self-hosted option removes this blocker.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Docker Compose deployment of cloud backend
- Helm chart for Kubernetes
- Self-hosted licence key model
- Full feature parity with cloud tier
label: infra

title: [E-04] Custom AI model configuration per org
description:
Some enterprises cannot send code context to Anthropic or OpenAI due to data policies. Custom model support removes the last adoption blocker.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Workspace-level AI provider config (overrides individual user config)
- Supports Azure OpenAI (data residency)
- Supports self-hosted models (Ollama on-prem, vLLM)
- Admin can restrict which providers members can use
label: feature

title: [E-05] Public API for third-party integrations
description:
Allow ecosystem tools to build on top of Workscribe data — custom dashboards, BI tools, HR systems.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- REST API with OAuth 2.0 client credentials
- Endpoints: sessions, summaries, team members, projects
- Rate limiting and API key management in dashboard
- API reference in docs
label: infra
